item.title: Popeyes to open new restaurant in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Popeyes to open new restaurant in King’s Lynn
A new Popeyes restaurant is coming to King’s Lynn. The fried chicken chain has confirmed it will take over the former Pizza Hut site at the Campbells Meadow retail park. While an official opening date has not yet been announced, the company says the new location will feature both dine-in facilities and park-and-serve bays for online orders.
The restaurant will serve the brand’s signature Louisiana-style chicken and buttermilk biscuits. Popeyes UK chief executive Tom Crowley said the company is looking forward to bringing its flavours to the local community. The chain, which was founded in 1972, has been expanding across the UK since 2021.

item.title: Further delays announced for Cambridgeshire local government shakeup
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Further delays announced for Cambridgeshire local government shakeup
Plans to reorganise local government in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough have faced further delays. The government has confirmed that the transition process, which aimed to replace existing district and county councils with new unitary authorities, will not proceed at this time.
While other regions have been selected to move forward, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough remain under review, with a further update expected by Christmas. The government has pledged £500,000 in transition funding to the area to help manage the costs of ongoing uncertainty. Local leaders have criticised the delay, describing the situation as a source of frustration for council staff, businesses, and residents who are seeking clarity on the future of local public services.
🔗 More details: https://www.fenlandcitizen.co.uk/news/local-government-shakeup-slammed-as-gut-punch-9489143/

item.title: Funding secured for new £600,000 fire training centre in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Funding secured for new £600,000 fire training centre in King’s Lynn
A new £600,000 specialist training facility is planned for the South Lynn fire station. The project is being funded by a joint investment of £300,000 each from Norfolk County Council and West Norfolk Council. The site will allow crews to practice for complex emergencies, including road traffic collisions and rescues at height, without needing to travel to other stations.
Construction is expected to begin next year, subject to planning consent and site surveys. Officials say the facility will help firefighters maintain vital skills locally and ensure emergency services can keep pace with the area's growing population. The development follows a record-breaking summer for Norfolk Fire and Rescue Service, which saw its busiest month on record this August.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Vehicle seized by police on the A47 in Wisbech
Police in Fenland have seized a van following a stop on the A47 near the Elm Hall roundabout in Wisbech. Officers from the local neighbourhood team pulled the vehicle over after noticing it was being driven with an exploded tyre.
Upon inspection, the driver was reported for several offences, including driving without a valid licence or insurance. They were also reported for operating a vehicle with an insecure load. The van has since been removed from the road.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Repairs approved for historic King’s Lynn South Gate
West Norfolk Council has granted listed building consent for maintenance work at the historic South Gate in King’s Lynn. The project includes replacing a window on the western side, installing a new internal timber screen, and repointing brickwork around the main gateway on London Road.
Architects state the repairs are necessary to prevent further degradation of the masonry and to keep the site secure. While the council has approved the plans, there is currently no confirmed start date for the work. It remains unclear if the repairs will require any traffic restrictions on London Road or what the total cost of the project will be. Historic England has expressed support for the proposed maintenance.
